title: Indus Valley sites in India
blurb: Harappan towns inside today's India. Harappa and Mohenjo-daro are in Pakistan, off this map.
source: Public facts (places and dates), listed by hand with the notes written for this site; positions taken from Wikidata where it has the place
licence: Facts, no copyright; positions from Wikidata (CC0)

items.name: Dholavira
items.detail: A city in Kutch with a chain of water reservoirs and a large inscription; a World Heritage Site since 2021.

items.name: Lothal
items.detail: A port town with a dockyard and a bead-making workshop.

items.name: Rakhigarhi
items.detail: One of the largest Harappan sites in India.

items.name: Kalibangan
items.detail: Known for a ploughed field of the early period and fire altars.

items.name: Banawali
items.detail: A Haryana site with early and mature Harappan levels.

items.name: Bhirrana
items.detail: A Haryana site with some of the earliest Harappan levels.

items.name: Surkotada
items.detail: A fortified Harappan site in Kutch.

items.name: Ropar
items.detail: The first Harappan site excavated in independent India (1950s), on the Sutlej.

items.name: Daimabad
items.detail: The southernmost site with Harappan links; known for a hoard of bronze figures.

items.name: Rangpur
items.detail: A Gujarat site on the Bhadar river with late Harappan levels.

items.name: Kuntasi
items.detail: A small port and workshop town on the Kutch coast.
